Disease Outbreak Disrupts Fisheries Workforce in Tulcea County

A disease outbreak has struck the fisheries industry in Romania's Tulcea County, causing significant operational challenges at several fish farms and processing sites along the Danube Delta. The outbreak, first identified last week, has led to a sharp increase in absenteeism among workers and has forced some facilities to suspend operations or reduce their processing capacity.

According to the Tulcea County Directorate of Fisheries, more than 120 workers across at least four major fisheries companies, including Delta Aqua and Sturionul Roșu, have reported symptoms consistent with acute gastroenteritis. Dr. Ioan Petrescu, the director of the Directorate, stated, “We are working closely with public health authorities to monitor the situation and ensure that affected workers receive appropriate care. Our main priority is the health and safety of the workforce.”

The outbreak has prompted immediate action from company management. “We have temporarily closed two of our processing lines and are conducting a thorough sanitation of our facilities,” said Elena Dumitru, spokesperson for Delta Aqua. “We are also providing regular health checks and additional protective equipment for staff who remain on-site.”

Production shortfalls have already begun to impact the industry’s operations in the region. Mihai Sandu, president of the Danube Fisheries Cooperative, noted, “Harvesting and processing have both slowed considerably. Our members report that daily output is down by up to 30% in some locations, and several sites are currently operating with half their usual workforce.”

Union representatives have voiced concern regarding the conditions that may have contributed to the outbreak. “Workers have been under intense pressure during the spring harvest,” said Anca Ionescu, chair of the Tulcea Fisheries Union. “We have requested a review of workplace hygiene practices and are urging all firms to prioritize employee health over output targets.”

While the source of the disease has not yet been determined, the Public Health Inspectorate is investigating possible links to communal facilities at several fish farms. Disinfection protocols have been intensified, and health authorities are conducting daily screenings of remaining staff.

Industry analysts warn that, should the outbreak continue, more severe production delays may follow. “Extended disruptions could affect the industry’s ability to meet domestic and export demand in the coming weeks,” said fisheries analyst Radu Stoica.

At present, the situation remains fluid as companies await further guidance from health officials. Many workers are still recovering at home, and management teams are preparing for a prolonged period of reduced operations if necessary.
